learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of material science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling the learning of new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knows the fundamental aspects of the structure of materials commonly used in Engineering.
Knows the main properties of various types of materials, as well as the relationships between them and their microstructural characteristics.
Knows how to perform basic mechanical tests and determine the mechanical properties of materials from them.
Knows how to apply knowledge of Materials Science to select the most suitable materials for applications in the field of industrial engineering.
Knows how to solve simple problems in the domain of Materials Science and Technology.

teaching_methods: Theory classes taught by the professor to the full group

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with short questions and problems (theory and problem classes content)
Written exam (laboratory session content, development, and experimental results)

assessment_rules: The course is evaluated through a global assessment via a single exam per call, consisting of two parts. The first test accounts for 70% of the final grade, requiring a minimum of 4 out of 10. The second test accounts for 30% of the final grade, also requiring a minimum of 4 out of 10. Failure to meet minimum scores in either test or using unauthorized materials may result in a failing grade.
